bull_bear.body:
- Disciplined / highly selective bidding — only contracts meeting return + margin thresholds.
- Maintains ~30% of targeted topline in cash; >INR 350 cr cash/FDs (~INR 300 cr free), partly lien-marked for bank guarantees.
- Pref capital raise completed; subsidiary capitalised via equity in proportion to holding (51%→75%).
- Conscious decision to hold short-term project debt (JNPT) alongside FDs earmarked for a specific vessel acquisition (avoid shortfall on capex).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Revenue-recognition lumpiness:** single-stage 100%-completion contracts create cost/revenue timing gaps (the Q4→Q1 ~INR 60 cr slip) — quarterly numbers will stay noisy; judge annually.
- **Seasonality:** Q1/Q2 (monsoon) structurally weak; H2-loaded.
- **Geopolitical:** Bahrain & Myanmar operations suspended (West Asia conflict / Myanmar instability) — overseas revenue idle until normalisation.
- **Execution / capex ambition:** INR 400–500 cr FY27 capex + new shipyard ramp + 14-vessel/yr export target are all unproven at scale.
- **Subsidy dependence:** shipbuilding margin leans on GoI 10–15% subsidy (25–30% without it).
- **Working capital / claims:** debtor days above target; INR 16 cr Mangrol claim still under discussion (no litigation, hopeful in FY27).
- **Funding:** large capex may need equity (dilution) if cash + debt insufficient / market-dependent.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - Founder-CEO (Sujay) detailed and confident; CFO (Kanak) handled balance-sheet questions directly. Candidly reframed the weak Q4 as a recognition-timing artifact (gave the exact INR 60 cr spill-over quantum and look-through margin). Conservative on guidance (annual not quarterly), prudent on capital (cash-first, retain 30% of topline in cash, won't risk vessels in unstable regions). Mild promotional tilt on the integrated-platform / "building an institution" narrative and on shipyard export optionality, but timelines hedged.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The Q4 "miss" is cosmetic: ~INR 60 cr of already-executed JNPA + Pondicherry dredging lands in Q1 FY27, so Q1 should print >INR 100 cr at >40% EBITDA — a setup for an optically strong next quarter.
- The Green Tug contracts (INR 650 cr, 15-yr) convert KMEW from lumpy project-bid revenue toward annuity-like recurring revenue — a structural re-rating lever if the Green Tug Transition Program scales.
- Backward integration is the real strategic pivot: owning the Saphale yard lets KMEW build its own green tugs + dredgers (capturing GoI subsidy + builder margin) instead of paying third-party builders — margin and capital-efficiency accretive.
- Tax structure is a quiet edge: tonnage-tax keeps the charter/dredging 80% of revenue at ~0% effective tax; only the growing 20% shipbuilding slice attracts corporate tax.
- River Pearl 47 is a moated asset — India's largest/deepest self-propelled backhoe dredger for hard-strata rock dredging that few competitors can do, with >240 days/yr utilisation visibility.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body:
- **Dredging (core):** capital + maintenance + rock/hard-strata. River Pearl 47 = India's largest & deepest self-propelled backhoe dredger, purpose-built for hard-strata rock dredging (10,000–500,000 m³ jobs) at New Mangalore, Mumbai, JNPA, Vizag, Tuticorin — mgmt sees >240 utilisation days/yr for next 2–3 yrs.
- **Marine chartering:** vessels chartered to GoI / ports / private entities — falls under tonnage-tax scheme.
- **Shipbuilding (Knowledge Shipyard, 51%→75%):** executing IWAI (Inland Waterways Authority of India) orders for cutter-suction dredgers + ancillary craft. New 15-acre Saphale (Palghar) yard near upcoming Vadhvan Port — designs vessels 10–120m LOA, ~20m beam, 5m draft (mooring/tug/survey boats, oil tankers, barges). Target 14 vessels/yr at full run-rate; marketing to European ship-owners/designers for exports. Equity-funded in proportion to holding.
- **Overseas:** Bahrain (sand-mining; vessel pulled out & redeployed to India — region risk, no evacuation/insurance comfort; FY26 ~INR 20 cr rev at negative margin) and Myanmar (no ongoing work; vessel redeployed to Port of Ghogha, Gujarat).

latest_quarter.body:
- Dredging/charter EBITDA 35–40%. Shipbuilding 25–30% pre-subsidy, 35–40% including GoI 10–15% subsidy (decision within ~60 days of application, applied per-vessel before construction).
- Tonnage-tax keeps effective tax near 0% on charter/dredging (tonnage tax <0.1% of chartering/dredging revenue); shipbuilding pays corporate tax.
- Fuel: bulk-fuel prices rose sharply (West Asia conflict) but all contracts have fuel pass-through → no negative impact.
- Q4 "other expenses" structurally higher (CSR concentrated in Q4 + insurance + new-vessel costs + JNPT/Pondicherry project costs).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this):** FY26 consol revenue ~INR 256 cr (+~27%), EBITDA ~INR 97 cr (~38%), PAT ~INR 79 cr (~31%, near-0% tax via tonnage). Record order book ~INR 1,400 cr; FY26 wins ~INR 1,075 cr (highest ever) incl. INR 650 cr / 15-yr Green Tug (VOCPA + Vizag). Q4 optically weak (~27% margin) on ~INR 60 cr JNPA+Pondicherry revenue slipping to Q1 FY27. Pipeline ~INR 2,000 cr (all domestic). FY27 capex guide INR 400–500 cr (~INR 100 cr shipyard). Saphale 15-acre yard acquired; Knowledge Shipyard 51%→75%. River Pearl 47 (India's largest backhoe dredger) commissioned.
- _Next Q (Q1 FY27) → check: (1) Q1 revenue >INR 100 cr at >40% EBITDA (the INR 60 cr spill-over recognised?); (2) ~INR 2,000 cr pipeline converting to orders within 3 months; (3) shipyard physical construction post-monsoon + green-tug build progress; (4) two larger dredgers / +12,000 m³ hopper added in <90 days; (5) debtor days toward 45–60 + INR 16 cr Mangrol claim recovered; (6) export small-craft order start (Q3/Q4); (7) Bahrain/Myanmar restart; (8) funding mix for INR 400–500 cr capex (equity dilution?)._

outlook.body:
- **Revenue growth:** ~30% YoY for next 2 years (FY27 & FY28). Annual guidance only — declined to give quarterly numbers (Q1/Q2 are seasonally low monsoon quarters; Q3/Q4 higher).
- **Margin:** Blended EBITDA 35–40% sustained; mgmt expects FY26 ~40% to nudge to 40–41% ("fair chance"). Margins should improve, not dip, despite shipyard pre-opex.
- **Q1 FY27:** Revenue >INR 100 cr (incl. the ~INR 60 cr spill-over) at EBITDA margin >40%.
- **Capex (FY27):** INR 400–500 cr — ~INR 100 cr on the Saphale shipyard, balance on acquiring dredgers + tugs. Two larger dredgers (+~12,000 m³ hopper capacity) could be added in <90 days; shipyard ~1 year to develop. Funding: cash first → debt → equity (only if needed).
- **Green tugs:** VOCPA + Vizag tugs built in-house at Saphale; physical construction post-monsoon, complete within ~9 months (i.e. through mid-monsoon CY27).
- **Shipbuilding mix:** FY27 ~20% of consol revenue from shipbuilding (corporate tax), ~80% dredging/charter (tonnage tax). Export orders for small craft expected to start Q3/Q4 FY27; yard at full run-rate = 14 vessels/yr.
- **Working capital:** Target debtor days 45–60 (currently above, skewed by one-off INR 16 cr claim).
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- Record order book ~INR 1,400 cr (dredging + charter-hire + shipbuilding). FY26 order wins ~INR 1,075 cr (highest ever).
- **Green Tug breakthrough:** two contracts — V.O.C. Port (Tuticorin) + Visakhapatnam Port — aggregating INR 650 cr, 15-year tenure. Long-duration recurring-revenue platform under India's Green Tug Transition Program (replacing diesel harbour tugs).
- **Bid pipeline ~INR 2,000 cr (all domestic):** dredging ~INR 950 cr + green tugs ~INR 600 cr + shipbuilding ~INR 400 cr; orders expected to flow over ~next 3 months. International orders deferred — will start adding overseas shipbuilding orders in Q3/Q4 FY27.
- **Execution profile:** Green Tug portion runs 15 years; balance order book executes over 2–3 years.
- **Recently executed:** JNPA rock-dredging (INR 50 cr, 3-month, underwater controlled drilling & blasting — used new asset River Pearl 47); 2 DCI capital-dredging contracts at Paradip (151,000 m³, INR 15 cr); DCI Pondicherry port maintenance dredging (restore to 5.0m/8.0m design depth).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Green Tug Transition Program** — KMEW among a select group of domestic players able to build green tugs; INR 650 cr signed + INR 600 cr in pipeline; scalable green-maritime-infra platform.
- **Backward integration into shipbuilding** — own yard reduces third-party dependence, improves capital efficiency, opens higher-margin value capture + GoI 10–15% construction subsidy.
- **Vessel exports** — small craft to Europe/neighbouring countries (orders expected Q3/Q4 FY27).
- **Hard-strata rock dredging niche** — River Pearl 47 addresses a scarce capability across 5 major ports.
- **Vadhvan Port adjacency** — Saphale yard strategically near the upcoming mega-port.

deepdive.thesis: KMEW is transitioning from an asset-operating dredging/charter contractor into an integrated maritime-infra platform that also builds its own vessels — FY26 consolidated revenue grew ~27% to ~INR 256 cr at a ~38% EBITDA margin, the order book hit a record ~INR 1,400 cr (incl. two 15-yr Green Tug contracts worth INR 650 cr), and management guides ~30% revenue growth for FY27/FY28 at 35–40% EBITDA. The optically weak Q4 (rev dip, ~27% margin) is a revenue-recognition artifact — ~INR 60 cr of completed JNPA + Pondicherry dredging billing slips into Q1 FY27 (single-stage 100%-completion payment), so the call is a "look-through, not a miss" quarter.

open.item: Q1FY27 revenue expected to be more than INR 100 crores (incl. ~INR 60 cr spilled over from Q4) with EBITDA margin improvement above 40%.
Near-term capex to buy 2 dredgers adding ~12,000 cubic meter hopper capacity, implementable in under 90 days.
FY27 capex of INR 400-500 crores, of which ~INR 100 cr on the shipyard and the balance on dredgers and tugs; INR 300 cr free cash available.
INR 16 crore outstanding claim from the Mangrol/DCI contract (of INR 24 cr, INR 8 cr received); two of three claims received, third expected in current financial year.
Current-year revenue mix expected at 20% shipbuilding (corporate tax) and 80% dredging/chartering (tonnage tax); tonnage tax not to exceed 0.1% of chartering/dredging revenue.
When fully functional, Saphale yard to build and deliver 14 vessels per year; export orders expected to start flowing in Q3 or Q4 FY27.
Developing 15-acre Saphale (Palghar) shipyard near Vadhvan Port; ~INR 100 cr capex, at least a year for full development.
FY27 capex funded from cash-in-hand and aligned debt first, with equity route considered only if needed; ~30% of top line kept as cash balance.
Aspiration to reach INR 500 crores revenue in the next 4-5 years and build a INR 1,000 crore market-cap company.

Two Green Tug contracts (VOCPA and Vishakhapatnam Port, INR 650 cr, 15-year tenure) to be built at Saphale yard; physical construction post-monsoon, completing within 9 months and fully constructed by mid-monsoon 2027.
Blended EBITDA margins to continue between 35% and 40%, with a fair chance of improving toward 40-41%.
Projecting revenue growth of 30% year-on-year for the next two years (FY27 and FY28).
Aim to reach 10% of the maintenance dredging market within three to four years (total dredging market ~INR 12,000 cr/annum).
River Pearl 47 (rock dredger) expected utilization in excess of 240 days per year for the next 2-3 years across five ports.
Plan to reach at least INR 1,000 crores top line within the decade.
Aim to own a fleet of 40-50+ vessels within the next 10 years (currently 12).
No operations currently in Bahrain (vessel redeployed to India) or Myanmar; to recommence once situations normalize.
Knowledge Marine's stake in the shipbuilding subsidiary (Knowledge Shipyard) to be raised from 51% to 75%; capital infused as equity in proportion to shareholding.
Shipbuilding EBITDA margin of 25-30% before subsidy, rising to 35-40% including the 10-15% government subsidy.
Actively exploring Saudi Arabia sand-mining business leveraging the Bahrain partner.
